content: Micro-fluidic chips have emerged as a novel tool for conducting chemical and biomedical processes in a miniaturized platform for the past two decades. Reagents can significantly decrease to micro-liters or nano-liters, and the reaction time could be shortened to a few seconds or less. One micro-fluidic subaggregate is a form of micro-droplet technology that can precisely manipulate mono-disperse micro-droplets, including their generation, fission, fusion, inside mixing, [double emulsion](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/multiple-emulsion "Learn more about double emulsion from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), sorting, and surface treatment. Micro-droplets have wide applications in micro-chemical reactors, targeting drug delivery, [biochemical](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/biochemicals "Learn more about biochemical from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") reactions, cell cultivation and encapsulation, and [protein crystallization](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/protein- crystallization "Learn more about protein crystallization from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"). Song et al. [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1359431115001659#bib1) recently reviewed biological and chemical reactions in droplets in micro- fluidic channels and reported the advantages and challenges in manipulating droplets as reactors and synthesis of micro-particles.
